target_customer: Enterprise contact centers on legacy on-premises phone systems (hospitality, retail chains, logistics, property management first; healthcare and financial services later)
problem: Enterprises running Cisco, Avaya or Mitel phone systems cannot easily adopt AI voice agents without migrating to the cloud, and want humans to stay in control of AI conversations.
business_model: B2B SaaS with managed deployment (agents built and implemented per customer); pricing plans page exists
product_category: AI voice and chat agents for contact centers with live human supervision

founders.name: Haithem Kchaou
previous_startups: Second-time founder; scaled a mobile app to 200K+ downloads (per YC page); earlier company Clusterlab per press
founders.background_notes: YC page: led a national AI initiative giving free LLM access to over 300,000 students, co-published 2 papers on LLM fine-tuning, Thomas Jefferson Scholar. Education and employers not listed.

founders.name: Chehir Dhaouadi
previous_startups: Co-built a mobile app with 200K+ downloads (per YC page)
founders.background_notes: YC page: software engineer who built and scaled telecom and VoIP systems across the Middle East and North Africa; trained over 300 developers. Employers not named.

competitors.name: Retell AI
competitors.what: AI voice agent platform for business phone systems; its own guide says it lacks deep supervisory and workforce tooling
competitors.traction_then: Established voice agent vendor with a published seed announcement

competitors.name: Cresta
competitors.what: Operations center for supervising many AI and human conversations with handoff context

competitors.name: Genesys, NICE CXone, Talkdesk
competitors.what: Incumbent CCaaS vendors adding voice AI to existing contact center offerings

technical_complexity.rationale: Real-time voice agents are standard with current LLM tooling, but running a carrier-grade telephony stack and native integration to Cisco, Avaya, Mitel and SIP trunks adds real engineering; the CTO has VoIP background.

defensibility.rationale: Many funded voice AI vendors and CCaaS incumbents compete; PBX integration and per-customer deployment add some switching cost but the AI layer is copyable.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: CCaaS incumbents were already adding voice AI in 2026; too early to know whether they absorb the wedge.

market_need_then: Voice AI adoption in contact centers was a hot category in 2026, and legacy PBX customers could not easily migrate to cloud; the company says it handles up to 70% of inbound calls (self reported).

branding.domain_note: Uses callab.ai; earlier or unrelated listings use callab.me

identity.voice_and_tone: Human-centered AI for CX teams; AI handles volume while people keep control

brand_strength.rationale: Only own site, directories and one regional press article found; name close to Calabrio and other similar names.

outcome_analysis: Callab AI is an active Spring 2026 YC company that grew out of the Tunisian and UAE company Clusterlab and sells AI voice agents that plug into legacy phone systems. Public funding information is limited to an unverified aggregator figure. It faces strong competition from voice AI startups and contact center incumbents, so its wedge is legacy PBX integration plus human supervision.
notes: Unverified: Neuronfeed lists total funding of $500K and a seed in March 2026; Seedtable lists last funding date 2026-04-01 with no amount. Only aggregators, so not recorded as a round. Founding year is 2024 per YC, 2025 per LinkedIn, 2020 per press for Clusterlab. YC launch post says P25 while profile says Spring 2026. Founder education and employers not listed on sources opened. Completeness pass: recorded a seed of 500K dated March 2026 resting on a single database (Neuronfeed). Seedtable gives a last funding date of 2026-04-01 with no amount, and no press release was found. Kchaou's earlier 600K pre-seed belongs to his other company Clusterlab, not Callab.
